Discussing the future of AI in Singapore and Asia: DBS conference

Advertisement

SINGAPORE – Bank executives, fund managers and start-up founders gathered at DBS Group's annual technology conference on Saturday to argue over how quickly artificial intelligence will reshape banking in the region.

The lender said its own AI models now screen most of its small-business loan applications, cutting the time to a decision from days to hours, and that it expects the savings to show up in its cost-to-income ratio over the next two years.

Analysts at the event were split on what that means for the shares. One fund manager said the bank's dividend, which has risen every year since 2020, remains the main reason investors own the stock; another warned that lower interest rates would squeeze its net interest margin in 2027.

Regulators also spoke. The Monetary Authority of Singapore said it would publish guidelines on the use of AI in credit decisions early next year, after a consultation that drew responses from all three local banks.
